requirements.title: A submodule extends a module or another submodule and has a host named by its parent identifier
requirements.definition: A submodule is a program unit extending a module or another submodule; the extended program unit is its host and is specified by the submodule statement parent identifier.

pending.submodule-host-is-parent-identifier: PENDING positive source plan: module m declares MODULE SUBROUTINE fill(x); submodule (m) sm implements it using host parameter base=17 and assigns x=22 to a caller variable initialized to -99, proving the parent identifier selects m as host rather than leaving the sentinel unchanged.
pending.submodule-can-extend-module-or-submodule: PENDING positive source plan: module m declares MODULE SUBROUTINE child_value(x); parent submodule (m) parent supplies a specification declaration parent_base=30; child submodule (m:parent) child implements child_value assigning x=31 from caller sentinel -31, proving the child host chain is usable.

requirements.title: Ancestor, descendant, and submodule identifier relationships are defined by the module-rooted tree
requirements.definition: A module or submodule is an ancestor program unit of its descendant submodules; a submodule identifier is the ordered pair of ancestor module name and submodule name, and the submodule name alone is not a local or global identifier.

pending.ordered-pair-submodule-identifier: PENDING positive source plan: modules a and b each declare a distinct separate module procedure and each has a submodule named impl; calls return exact 14 and 23 respectively, demonstrating that (a,impl) and (b,impl) are distinct identifiers.
pending.submodule-name-not-local-or-global-ident: PENDING source-admission plan: use identical submodule-name impl under two different ancestor modules with exact procedure results 14 and 23; no test treats impl alone as callable or externally linkable.

requirements.title: A submodule may implement separate module procedures declared in itself or an ancestor
requirements.source: 14.2.3 p3 separate module procedure permission; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023 PDF p321.
requirements.definition: A submodule is permitted to provide implementations for separate module procedures declared within that submodule or within one of its ancestors.

requirements.title: Submodule declarations and definitions can be host associated into descendant submodules
requirements.source: 14.2.3 p3 descendant host-association effect; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023 PDF p321.
requirements.definition: A submodule can contain declarations and definitions of entities that are accessible by host association in its descendant submodules.

requirements.title: Submodule specification parts cannot contain FORMAT, ENTRY, or statement-function statements
requirements.definition: A submodule specification part shall not contain a format statement, entry statement, or statement-function statement.

pending.format-stmt-forbidden-in-submodule-spec: PENDING diagnostic/control pair: negative places `100 FORMAT(I0)` in the submodule specification part; control moves the same FORMAT statement into the contained MODULE PROCEDURE body and keeps the same interface and exact result.
pending.entry-stmt-forbidden-in-submodule-spec: PENDING diagnostic/control pair: negative places `ENTRY alternate()` in the submodule specification part; control removes only that ENTRY statement, leaving the same parent module, submodule name, declarations, and module procedure body with exact result 13. The control is checked to keep all declarations before executable statements and not rely on ENTRY being valid in a module procedure.

requirements.title: Submodule parent identifiers must name a nonintrinsic ancestor module with a separate module procedure and a descendant parent submodule
requirements.definition: The ancestor module name in a parent identifier shall name a nonintrinsic module that declares a separate module procedure; the parent submodule name shall name a descendant of that module.

pending.ancestor-module-declares-separate-module: PENDING diagnostic/control pair: negative uses a nonintrinsic local module m with no separate module procedure declaration as the ancestor in SUBMODULE (m) s; control adds only one matching MODULE SUBROUTINE interface in the same module m and keeps the submodule implementing it with the same exact result. The nonintrinsic wording is subsumed here: an intrinsic module cannot declare a separate module procedure, so an intrinsic-module negative would also change this feature and is not isolated.
pending.parent-submodule-is-descendant: PENDING diagnostic/control pair: negative names a sibling or absent parent submodule in SUBMODULE (m:wrong_parent) child; control changes only the parent-submodule-name to the actual descendant parent and preserves exact result 36.
